deities: Goddess Pashan Devi (Nav Durga - the nine forms of Durga, worshipped as nine stone pindis)
festivals: Navratri (March-April and September-October; the temple's biggest gathering)

history.period: Ancient; said to date from the origin of Naini Lake (no documentary evidence - verify)
history.summary: One of Nainital's oldest and most revered shrines, on Thandi Sadak at Tallital on the northern shore of Naini Lake. 'Pashan' means stone: the goddess is worshipped as a naturally formed stone figure and as nine stone pindis representing the Nav Durga, carved on the rock face by the lake. An Akhand Jyoti (eternal flame) is said to have burned continuously since the temple's formation. Local belief holds the goddess protects the region and cures skin diseases and speech ailments like stammering; offered water flows down to Naini Lake after touching the deity's feet. A legend tells of an Englishman who mocked the small shrine and fell with his horse into the lake until he sought forgiveness. A recent idol of Baba Neem Karoli Maharaj has also been installed in the complex. No firm construction date is documented; sources attribute its origin to the lake's own antiquity.

name: Pashan Devi Temple
town_description: Nainital is a lakeside hill station in the Kumaon region of Uttarakhand at about 2,084 m, built around the pear-shaped Naini Lake. Once the summer capital of the United Provinces under the British, it is one of India's most visited hill towns, known for Mall Road, the Naina Devi Shakti Peetha, Tiffin Top, and panoramic Himalayan views.

travel.airport: Pantnagar Airport, the nearest airport (~70 km from Nainital); taxis and buses connect to the town
travel.railway: Kathgodam railway station, the nearest railhead (~35 km from Nainital), with trains from Delhi, Kolkata and Lucknow; taxis/buses onward
travel.road: The temple is at Tallital on Thandi Sadak, reached on foot (no vehicular traffic on the stretch); Nainital is ~300 km from Delhi by road via Kathgodam-Haldwani

visitor_information.best_time: March to June and September to November (pleasant weather); open year-round
visitor_information.opening_hours: No published hours (verify); typically open dawn to dusk - confirm locally
